prompt: A streaming service raised its price by 15%. Subscribers fell by 3% in the following quarter. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Subscribers probably fell 3% because the price rose 15%.
options.feedback: This repeats the facts as if they were the answer. It doesn't say what they mean for revenue, which is the question that matters.

options.text: Demand probably barely reacts to price, so revenue likely rose.
options.feedback: Right. About 1.15 × 0.97 ≈ 1.12, so revenue likely rose about 11%. I'd check revenue and cancellations by plan before and after.

options.text: The price rise worked, so a second increase will work too.
options.feedback: This treats one result as certain and assumes the next increase will behave the same way.

options.text: Most subscribers have likely cancelled or paused since the increase.

explanation: The data shows price up 15% and subscribers down 3%, so revenue rose about 11% (1.15 × 0.97). Likely cause: demand is price-insensitive. To test it, track revenue and cancellations by plan for more than one quarter. If cancellations keep climbing, the gain will shrink.
